questions.stem: Which combination of features best distinguishes a living thing from a non-living thing?
options: It responds to heat and dissolves in water
It is made of cells, uses energy, grows and reproduces
It moves, changes shape and contains water
It contains carbon, takes up space and has mass
questions.explanation: Living things share a set of characteristics: they are made of one or more cells, carry out metabolism using energy, grow, respond to stimuli and reproduce. Movement and water content alone do not separate life from non-life, since a flowing river moves and contains water.

questions.stem: A student argues that a candle flame is alive because it 'feeds' on wax, uses oxygen, releases carbon dioxide and can 'grow'. Which feature of living things does the flame clearly lack?
options: It is not made of cells and has no hereditary material
It does not use oxygen or release any waste gases
It cannot change in size as conditions change
It does not release energy as heat or light
questions.explanation: A flame shares some features with life, such as using oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide, but it has no cells and no hereditary material to pass on. The flame does use oxygen and releases gases, so those features do not separate it from living things.

questions.stem: Which statement is part of the cell theory?
options: All cells come from pre-existing cells
All cells contain a nucleus and chloroplasts
Cells can form from non-living matter today
Only multicellular organisms are made of cells
questions.explanation: The cell theory states that living things are made of one or more cells, that cells are the structural and functional units of life, that cells come from pre-existing cells and that cells contain hereditary material. Not all cells have a nucleus or chloroplasts, and unicellular organisms are made of cells too.

questions.stem: Cellulose tubing containing starch solution is placed in a beaker of yellow-brown iodine solution. After 20 minutes the liquid inside the tubing is blue-black but the liquid outside is still yellow-brown. What can be concluded?
options: Starch crossed the tubing but iodine molecules did not
Both starch and iodine crossed the tubing in equal amounts
Water crossed the tubing but neither solute did at all
Iodine crossed the tubing but starch molecules did not
questions.explanation: The blue-black colour forms where starch meets iodine. It appeared only inside, so the small iodine molecules diffused in, while the large starch molecules could not get out, as the outside liquid did not change colour. The tubing models a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.stem: Viruses contain nucleic acid and protein but can only reproduce inside a host cell. Why does the cell theory not treat viruses as cells?
options: They are made mainly of lipids rather than proteins
They have no cell membrane, cytoplasm or ribosomes of their own
They contain no hereditary material of any kind
They are larger than most bacteria and eukaryotic cells
questions.explanation: A cell is defined by its membrane, which separates it from its surroundings, and it has its own cytoplasm and ribosomes for making proteins. Viruses lack these, so they cannot carry out life processes independently. They do carry hereditary material (DNA or RNA), so that is not the reason.

questions.stem: What structure defines a cell by separating it from its surroundings?
options: The cell membrane
The cell wall
The nucleus
The cytoskeleton network
questions.explanation: Every cell is bounded by a cell membrane that separates its contents from the external environment. Cell walls are found only in some cells (plants, fungi and most bacteria), and prokaryotes have no nucleus.

questions.stem: Which set of features is found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Cell wall, chloroplasts, nucleic acids and proteins
Golgi body, ribosomes, nucleus and nucleic acids
Cell membrane, nucleic acids, proteins and ribosomes
Nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes and cell membrane
questions.explanation: All cells have a cell membrane, nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), proteins and ribosomes, a reflection of their common evolutionary past. Prokaryotes lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and the Golgi body.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of a prokaryotic cell?
options: A diameter of about 50 to 100 micrometres
A single circular chromosome free in the cytoplasm
Several linear chromosomes inside a nucleus
Membrane-bound mitochondria and chloroplasts
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells usually have one circular chromosome in the cytoplasm, with no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. They are typically about 1 to 10 micrometres across, much smaller than eukaryotic cells.

questions.stem: A cell is viewed under an electron microscope. It is 2 micrometres long, has ribosomes and a cell wall, but has no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. What type of cell is it most likely to be?
options: A plant leaf cell
A yeast cell
A human white blood cell
A bacterial cell
questions.explanation: The small size and lack of a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles identify a prokaryote, such as a bacterium. Yeast cells also have a cell wall, but they are eukaryotic fungi with a nucleus and mitochondria.

questions.stem: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells both have ribosomes, a cell membrane and DNA. What is the best explanation for these shared features?
options: Both cell types live in the same environments
Prokaryotes take these structures from eukaryotes
Both cell types evolved from a common ancestral cell
Eukaryotic cells evolved first and later lost these features
questions.explanation: Features shared by all cells reflect their common evolutionary past: they were inherited from a common ancestor. Living in the same environment would not explain identical molecular machinery such as ribosomes, and prokaryotes appeared before eukaryotes.

questions.stem: A student examines two cell types. Cell P is about 1 micrometre across with no nucleus. Cell Q is about 20 micrometres across with a nucleus and many organelles. Which statement is correct?
options: Cell P must be a virus because it has no nucleus
Cell P cannot make proteins because it lacks organelles
Cell Q will have a single circular chromosome
Cell Q has internal membranes that separate different reactions
questions.explanation: Cell Q is eukaryotic, and its membrane-bound organelles compartmentalise reactions. Cell P is a prokaryote, which still makes proteins on its ribosomes; ribosomes are not membrane-bound. Viruses are not cells, and eukaryotes have several linear chromosomes in the nucleus.

questions.stem: What must a cell do before it divides into two daughter cells?
options: Copy its genetic material
Halve its number of chromosomes
Break down its cell membrane
Fuse with another cell
questions.explanation: Before dividing, a cell copies (replicates) its DNA so that each daughter cell receives a full set of genetic material. Halving the chromosome number happens only in meiosis, not in ordinary cell division.

questions.stem: How do bacteria reproduce?
options: By meiosis
By meiosis and fertilisation
By binary fission
By mitosis
questions.explanation: Bacteria divide by binary fission: the circular chromosome is copied, the copies move apart as the cell elongates, and the cell splits in two. Mitosis is the division of the nucleus in eukaryotic cells, and prokaryotes have no nucleus.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares binary fission and mitosis?
options: Binary fission occurs in the nucleus, while mitosis occurs in the cytoplasm
Binary fission involves no spindle, while mitosis separates chromosomes on a spindle
Binary fission produces four cells, while mitosis produces two cells
Binary fission halves the chromosome number, while mitosis keeps it constant
questions.explanation: In binary fission the single circular chromosome is copied and the copies separate as the cell grows, without a spindle. In mitosis, many linear chromosomes in the nucleus are separated by a spindle. Both produce two genetically identical cells with the parent's chromosome number.

questions.stem: During which phase of mitosis do the chromosomes line up across the middle (equator) of the cell?
options: Telophase
Metaphase
Prophase
Anaphase
questions.explanation: In metaphase the chromosomes line up on the equator, attached to spindle fibres. In prophase they condense, in anaphase the sister chromatids are pulled apart, and in telophase new nuclear membranes form.

questions.stem: A student looking at an onion root tip sees a cell in which sister chromatids are being pulled towards opposite ends of the cell. Which phase of mitosis is this?
options: Anaphase
Metaphase
Prophase
Telophase
questions.explanation: Anaphase is when spindle fibres pull sister chromatids apart to opposite poles. In metaphase the chromosomes are still lined up at the equator, not yet separated.

questions.stem: A human skin cell has 46 chromosomes. It divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes does each daughter cell have?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent, each with the same number of chromosomes, 46. Halving to 23 occurs only when gametes are made by meiosis.

questions.stem: Human body cells are diploid and human egg cells are haploid. What does this mean?
options: Body cells have one set of chromosomes; egg cells have two sets
Body cells have 23 chromosomes; egg cells have 46 chromosomes
Body cells divide by fission; egg cells divide by mitosis
Body cells have two sets of chromosomes; egg cells have one set
questions.explanation: Diploid cells (2n) have two sets of chromosomes, one from each parent; in humans 2n = 46. Haploid cells (n) such as eggs and sperm have one set, 23 in humans.

questions.stem: What is the main source of energy for most autotrophs?
options: Heat from the soil
Oxygen in the air
Light
Glucose eaten as food
questions.explanation: Most autotrophs, such as plants and algae, capture light energy in photosynthesis. Heterotrophs get chemical energy from the food they consume.

questions.stem: Which word equation represents photosynthesis?
options: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water
glucose -> ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose -> lactic acid
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. The reverse equation is aerobic respiration, and the other two are fermentation in yeast or plants and in animals.

questions.stem: Which word equation represents aerobic respiration?
options: glucose + carbon dioxide -> oxygen + water
glucose -> lactic acid + carbon dioxide
glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water
carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
questions.explanation: In aerobic respiration, glucose reacts with oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water. Photosynthesis is the reverse process and stores energy in glucose.

questions.stem: A sprinter's leg muscle cells run short of oxygen. Which word equation shows how they continue to release some energy?
options: glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water
lactic acid -> glucose + oxygen
glucose -> lactic acid
glucose -> ethanol + carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Without enough oxygen, animal cells carry out fermentation (anaerobic respiration), converting glucose to lactic acid. Yeast and plant cells instead produce ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Bread dough containing yeast rises when left in a warm place. Which word equation explains why?
options: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
glucose + oxygen -> ethanol + water
glucose -> ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose -> lactic acid
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars in the dough to ethanol and carbon dioxide, and the carbon dioxide gas forms bubbles that make the dough rise. Lactic acid is the fermentation product in animal cells and produces no gas.

questions.stem: A sealed flask contains yeast in glucose solution with no oxygen. Which pair of measurements would best show that fermentation is occurring?
options: Oxygen is released and glucose concentration rises
Lactic acid accumulates and no gas is released
Water is produced and oxygen is used up
Carbon dioxide is released and ethanol accumulates
questions.explanation: Yeast fermentation converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide, so gas output and rising ethanol confirm it. Lactic acid without gas is fermentation in animal cells, and using oxygen to make water is aerobic respiration, which cannot occur without oxygen.

questions.stem: Which comparison of the material needs of autotrophs and heterotrophs is correct?
options: Autotrophs take in carbon dioxide and mineral ions; heterotrophs take in organic food
Autotrophs take in organic food; heterotrophs take in carbon dioxide and mineral ions
Both take in glucose from their surroundings as their carbon source
Autotrophs need no oxygen; heterotrophs need no water
questions.explanation: Autotrophs build their own organic molecules from inorganic materials such as carbon dioxide, water and mineral ions. Heterotrophs must obtain ready-made organic molecules by eating other organisms. Autotrophs still use oxygen in respiration.

questions.stem: Why must cells remove waste products such as carbon dioxide and ammonia?
options: Wastes stop the cell from copying its DNA before division
Wastes can build up to toxic levels and disrupt cell reactions
Wastes are needed by the cell's neighbours for photosynthesis
Wastes make the cell membrane fully permeable to all molecules
questions.explanation: Accumulated wastes can change conditions inside the cell, such as pH, and some, like ammonia, are toxic, which disrupts enzymes and cell reactions. Removing them keeps internal conditions relatively constant.

questions.stem: During the day a leaf cell carries out both photosynthesis and respiration. Which substance does a leaf cell release as a waste in bright light?
options: Oxygen
Glucose
Mineral ions
Starch
questions.explanation: In bright light, photosynthesis produces more oxygen than respiration uses, so excess oxygen diffuses out of the leaf. Glucose and starch are kept as food and energy stores.

questions.stem: What are the two main kinds of molecule that make up the cell membrane?
options: Cellulose and starch
Nucleic acids and simple sugars
Glycogen and cellulose fibres
Phospholipids and proteins
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it or attached to it. Cellulose forms plant cell walls, and starch and glycogen are storage carbohydrates.

questions.stem: Why is the cell membrane described as selectively permeable?
options: It lets some substances cross but not others
It lets all small and large molecules cross freely
It is completely impermeable to water
It only allows substances to leave the cell
questions.explanation: A selectively permeable membrane lets some substances through, such as water, oxygen and carbon dioxide, while restricting others such as large or charged molecules. This control helps the cell keep its internal conditions relatively constant.

questions.stem: What is diffusion?
options: Movement of water only, across a selectively permeable membrane
Engulfing of large particles by the cell membrane
Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
Net movement of particles from low to high concentration using energy
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient, from high to low concentration, and needs no energy input from the cell. Movement against the gradient is active transport, and osmosis refers specifically to water.

questions.stem: A red blood cell is placed in pure water. What happens and why?
options: Nothing happens because the membrane is impermeable to water
Water enters by osmosis and the cell swells and may burst
Water leaves by osmosis and the cell shrinks
Salt enters by diffusion and the cell shrinks
questions.explanation: Pure water has a higher water concentration than the cell's cytoplasm, so water moves into the cell by osmosis. Animal cells have no cell wall, so the cell swells and can burst.

questions.stem: Rhubarb epidermal cells are placed in a concentrated sugar solution and viewed under a microscope. What will be observed?
options: The cell walls collapse inwards as sugar diffuses out
The cells stay unchanged because the wall blocks all water
The cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall as water leaves
The cells swell and burst as sugar enters by osmosis
questions.explanation: The sugar solution has a lower water concentration than the cell contents, so water leaves by osmosis and the cytoplasm and membrane pull away from the rigid cell wall (plasmolysis). Osmosis is the movement of water, not sugar, and the wall prevents bursting rather than blocking water.

questions.stem: How does active transport differ from diffusion?
options: It moves substances against the gradient and needs no energy
It moves substances against the concentration gradient and needs energy
It moves substances down the concentration gradient and needs energy
It moves only water and needs no energy
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy (from respiration) and carrier proteins to move substances from low to high concentration. Diffusion and osmosis are passive: they move substances down the gradient with no energy input from the cell.

questions.stem: Root hair cells contain potassium ions at a much higher concentration than the surrounding soil water. If a poison stops respiration in the roots, uptake of potassium stops. What does this show?
options: Potassium uptake depends only on the rate of photosynthesis
Potassium is taken up by active transport using energy from respiration
Potassium is taken up by diffusion down its concentration gradient
Potassium is taken up by osmosis along with water
questions.explanation: Uptake against a concentration gradient that stops when respiration stops must depend on energy, which identifies active transport. Diffusion would move potassium out of the root, down its gradient, and osmosis is the movement of water.

questions.stem: A cube-shaped cell has sides of 2 micrometres. What is its surface area-to-volume ratio?
questions.explanation: Surface area = 6 x 2 x 2 = 24 square micrometres. Volume = 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cubic micrometres. 24 : 8 simplifies to 3 : 1.

questions.stem: Agar cubes of side 1 cm, 2 cm and 3 cm containing an indicator are placed in acid for 5 minutes. Which result is expected, and why?
options: The 2 cm cube changes colour most completely because it is a medium size
The 1 cm cube changes colour most completely because it has the largest SA:V ratio
The 3 cm cube changes colour most completely because it has the largest surface area
All cubes change colour to the same extent because acid diffuses at one rate
questions.explanation: Acid diffuses in at about the same distance per minute in each cube, so the smallest cube, with an SA:V of 6 : 1 compared with 3 : 1 and 2 : 1, has the greatest proportion of its volume reached. A larger total surface area does not make up for the much larger volume.

questions.stem: Why is it an advantage for a cell to stay small?
options: A small cell has a smaller surface area-to-volume ratio for exchange
A small cell can only contain one chromosome
A small cell has a large surface area-to-volume ratio for exchange
A small cell needs no materials from its surroundings
questions.explanation: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area, so its SA:V ratio falls. Small cells have a large SA:V ratio, so their membrane can exchange materials fast enough to supply the whole volume.

questions.stem: A spherical cell doubles in diameter. Which statement about its surface area-to-volume ratio is correct?
options: The ratio stays the same because both measures double
The ratio falls to one-eighth because volume rises eightfold
The ratio halves, so exchange per unit volume becomes less efficient
The ratio doubles, so exchange per unit volume becomes more efficient
questions.explanation: Doubling the diameter multiplies surface area by 4 and volume by 8, so SA:V becomes 4/8, half its original value. Volume rising eightfold alone does not set the ratio, because surface area also rises fourfold.
